The '''Imperial Prison Transport''' ('''IPT''') was a modified version of the [[Imperial Troop Transport]] to serve as a [[prisoner]] [[transport]], ferrying prisoners to [[prison]]s such as [[Imperial factory facility|Imperial factory facilities]]. The repurposed IPT stripped the comforts of the base transport model and added new restraints, with the prisoner passenger cabin located on the starboard side. The IPT additionally kept life support systems at the bare minimum, and the [[cockpit]] was physically separated from the prisoner hold. The [[Ion engine|ion sublight drives]] were supported by struts.<ref name="SW DORVG" />

In [[5 BBY]],<ref name="Date">{{AndorDate|108}}</ref> [[Cassian Jeron Andor]] was arrested on [[Niamos]], and was led to an area outside of the [[Niamos Courthouse]] along with other prisoners where three IPTs were loading them to transport the prisoners to different locations. Andor was placed into an IPT which ferried him and a number of others to a [[Unidentified Imperial factory facility|facility]] on [[Narkina 5]] part of the massive<ref name="SWE TCGSWG" /> [[Narkina 5 Imperial Prison Complex]].<ref name="Narkina 5" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Imperial Prison Transport (IPT) first appeared in the [[Disney+]] live-action television series, ''[[Star Wars: Andor]]'s'', [[Andor Season 1|first season]], within the episode "[[Narkina 5 (episode)|Narkina 5]]".<ref name="Narkina 5" /> The design of the IPT was confirmed to be based upon the Imperial Troop Transport (ITT),<ref name="IPTDesignBasedOnITT">{{SW|url=andor-s1-e8-trivia-gallery|text=Andor | Season 1, Episode 8 - Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Image 4}}.</ref> which made its debut prior in the Disney+ live-action television series ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]''.<ref name="Chapter 14">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 14: The Tragedy}}</ref> The reference book ''[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]]'', released on [[November 2]], [[2023]] in the United Kingdom, codified this through establishing it to be a retrofitted version of the ITT, denoted as the 'Imperial Prison Transport'.<ref name="SW DORVG" />
